headline: Anthropic's annualized revenue surges to $65B, outpacing OpenAI's growth
summary: Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate reportedly hit $65 billion by July, up from $47 billion in May and $9 billion last year, showcasing rapid acceleration in the AI market.
details: Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate reportedly surpassed $65 billion by the end of July, according to Bloomberg. This marks a significant acceleration from $47 billion in May and just $9 billion at the end of last year.
Investors anticipate continued rapid growth, with projections placing Anthropic's revenue between $100 billion and $120 billion by the end of 2026, as reported by the Financial Times.
In comparison, rival OpenAI recently doubled its revenue to $40 billion. While metrics may differ, Anthropic's growth rate has reportedly garnered more investor attention.
Both companies have filed confidential IPO paperwork. Anthropic is expected to go public ahead of OpenAI, possibly as soon as this fall, seeking a public valuation of $2 trillion or more.
This potential valuation would make it the largest market debut on record. Anthropic was last privately valued at $965 billion in late May after a $65 billion funding round.
caption:
Anthropic's annualized revenue has reportedly soared to $65 billion by July, a massive leap from $9 billion at the end of last year. This rapid growth is captivating investors.

Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate reportedly surpassed $65 billion by the end of July, according to Bloomberg. This marks a significant acceleration from $47 billion in May and just $9 billion at the end of last year.

Investors anticipate continued rapid growth, with projections placing Anthropic's revenue between $100 billion and $120 billion by the end of 2026, as reported by the Financial Times.

In comparison, rival OpenAI recently doubled its revenue to $40 billion. While metrics may differ, Anthropic's growth rate has reportedly garnered more investor attention.

Both companies have filed confidential IPO paperwork. Anthropic is expected to go public ahead of OpenAI, possibly as soon as this fall, seeking a public valuation of $2 trillion or more.

This potential valuation would make it the largest market debut on record. Anthropic was last privately valued at $965 billion in late May after a $65 billion funding round.

headline_marked: [[Cursor launches Origin code hosting platform]] as GitHub suffers global outage
headline: Cursor launches Origin code hosting platform as GitHub suffers global outage
summary: Cursor's new platform rolled out just hours before GitHub experienced a near 7-hour global degradation, exposing a potential market opening for AI-powered code hosting.
details: Cursor officially launched Origin, its new code hosting platform for paid users, on Monday morning. Just hours later, GitHub experienced a global degradation lasting over six hours, with error rates reaching 20-50% across key services like pull requests and API calls.

The outage also affected GitHub Copilot and enterprise single sign-on, leading to widespread disruption. Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch highlighted the irony, noting Origin was online while GitHub was down, despite Vercel itself being impacted.

The timing, though coincidental, dramatically underscored Origin's core premise: AI agents are making code hosting a critical decision again. Cursor is betting that technical decision-makers will now re-evaluate their source code management.

Origin integrates directly into Cursor's editor via a new Codebase tab, providing expected forge machinery like Git wrapping, storage, permissions, and merge handling. It includes pull requests with timelines, commits, and file changes, all viewable within the editor.

A key feature is the integration of AI agents that operate directly within the code and pull request interface. Developers can ask questions, have agents revise pull requests, or push branches, all without leaving their editor.

Day-one integrations include Vercel for preview deployments and production shipping, plus Depot and Buildkite for continuous integration. Crucially, both CI partners can execute existing GitHub Actions workflows without modification.

This compatibility layer is central to Cursor's strategy, aiming to avoid disruptive "rip-and-replace" migrations. Instead, it offers teams a "second window" onto their existing code, making adoption significantly easier.

Origin doesn't require users to abandon GitHub; it connects to GitHub organizations, mirroring existing access permissions. Pushes continue to GitHub as the source of truth, and pull request conversations sync bi-directionally in real-time.

This "wedge" strategy allows teams to gradually integrate Origin without the high risks associated with migrating entire source control systems. It presents a less daunting path for enterprises to explore AI-powered code management.
